# Sum of balls, two-limb center, finite core

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_add_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, that contains $x + y$ for every $x \in X, y \in Y$, with $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x + y : x \in X, y \in Y \,\}.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c_x = c_{x0} + c_{x1}$, $c_y = c_{y0} + c_{y1}$, $c_z = c_{z0} + c_{z1}$.

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet. The operations of the public headers call [`ball_add_2_full`](ball_add_2_full.md), which computes this kernel and then the fix-up of its results.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $c_x$ is normalized: $c_{x0} = \mathrm{RN}(c_{x0} + c_{x1})$.
- $r_x \ge 0$.
- $c_y$ is normalized: $c_{y0} = \mathrm{RN}(c_{y0} + c_{y1})$.
- $r_y \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $c_z$ is normalized: $c_{z0} = \mathrm{RN}(c_{z0} + c_{z1})$.
- $\lvert (x + y) - c_z\rvert \le r_z$ for all real $x$ and $y$ with $\lvert x - c_x\rvert \le r_x$, $\lvert y - c_y\rvert \le r_y$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_add_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Ball2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Ball2.v), against `ball_add_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_add_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition ball_add_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (3 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall cx0 cx1 rx cy0 cy1 ry : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec cx0 cx1 ->
  fmt emin prec rx ->
  normalized_2 emin prec cy0 cy1 ->
  fmt emin prec ry ->
  0 <= rx ->
  0 <= ry ->
  let '(cz0, cz1, rz) := ball_add_2 emin prec tie_even cx0 cx1 rx cy0 cy1 ry in
  fmt emin prec rz /\
  normalized_2 emin prec cz0 cz1 /\
  (forall x y : R, Rabs (x - (cx0 + cx1)) <= rx -> Rabs (y - (cy0 + cy1)) <= ry -> Rabs ((x + y) - (cz0 + cz1)) <= rz).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_add_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** midpoint-radius sum (Milestone 1 listing, second radius design). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_add_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_add_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`add_2_2`](add_2_2.md).

```
# The sum of two balls with 2-limb centers: the center by add_2_2, the radius in the second design.
# The radius is evaluated by operations rounded to nearest on nonnegative values and inflated
# once (milestone1.md, "The radius, second design"): E turns the error bound of the center
# kernel add_2_2 into a multiple of |cz0|, G covers the roundings of the radius, H what underflow
# loses and the absolute term of the bound. Each is an exact expression rounded up. H also
# contains eta/(2u), the smallest normal number, which no bound needs: it makes H, and with it
# every radius a kernel returns, a normal number, because a fused operation with a subnormal
# operand is slow on some processors (decisions.md, the log of 2026-11-19).

(cz0, cz1)  = add_2_2(cx0, cx1, cy0, cy1)
az          = abs(cz0)
s           = add(rx, ry)
t           = fma(az, const up(unit(add_2_2)/(1-unit(add_2_2))*(1+u)), s)
rz          = fma(t, const up((1+u)^3), const up((1+u)*((1+u)^2*eta+eta/2)+eta/(2*u)))
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 1**: the runs of commit `6f89054`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#ball_add_2)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | smallest slack of the radius, in gaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 104 519 064 | 0 | 1.25238 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 104 442 504 | 0 | 1.25013 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 4 formats | 39 929 434 | 0 | 1.25 (`fp:3:-3:2`) |

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_add_2)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | smallest slack of the radius, in gaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 6 670 062 | 0 | 1.28825 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 6 667 956 | 0 | 1.25548 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 4 formats | 39 929 434 | 0 | 1.25 (`fp:3:-3:2`) |

**In all**, the runs above:

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled, Milestone 1 and Milestone 2 | 111 189 126 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled, Milestone 1 and Milestone 2 | 111 110 460 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand of 5 distinct domains, each counted once, Milestone 1 and Milestone 2 | 39 929 434 | 0 |

The slack is how far the returned radius is above the smallest radius that encloses the exact set, in units in the last place of the radius: below 1, a radius one unit smaller would not enclose it.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: [`ball_add_2_full`](ball_add_2_full.md) states that ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values) says what the library does now).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
